title: Belief blame: blame the assumption, not the author
status: PROPOSED, ethereal stage, nothing built; propose-only, Zach rules
one_line: git blame says who last touched a line. Belief blame says which assumption the line encodes, the commit it entered in, which evidence later shifted it, and whether the line is still current or is now a known blindspot. Point it at any line of a process file (AGENTS.md, _PATTERNS, _DECISIONS, .claude/rules, script headers) or any backlog depends_on edge.

bottom_line.label: The idea (Zach, 2026-11-01)
bottom_line.text: "what if our blame was process assumptions or dependancies or blindspots that changed over time based on observed new evidence that shifted our beliefs". The thing blamed is a belief and the evidence that moved it, not a person.

bottom_line.label: What the trace found
bottom_line.text: A hand trace of the first real line (AGENTS.md gotcha 17), done the way the tool would, found a live blindspot: the belief "branch protection cannot enforce this on the free plan, so detection, not prevention" was rewritten in AGENTS.md on 2026-10-06 (1c798b7b), but the same sentence still stands in scripts/squash_merge_detector.py line 7. It also found a relapse: falsification row F26 (2026-07-24, a merge went through on a red check) and the safe_merge.sh Tuition (2026-10-20, a merge went through on a PENDING check) are the same belief failing twice, and the later record does not cite the earlier one.

bottom_line.label: Why git blame alone is wrong here
bottom_line.text: git blame -w -C on gotcha 17 credits 51ddf069 (2026-10-20, safe_merge.sh). The never-squash belief entered on 2026-09-28 (0df06046). Blame gives the last rewording; belief blame must walk the line's history (git log -L, then git log -S on the quoted phrase) to the first commit that stated the assumption.

bottom_line.label: What it adds
bottom_line.text: One optional field, anchors, on falsification-ledger and assumptions rows (path plus a quoted phrase, never a line number). One read-only script that joins line to commit to assumption to evidence and prints a verdict. No new store, no model calls. Everything else already exists.

decisions.question: Add an optional anchors field to _STATE/falsification-ledger.jsonl and _STATE/assumptions.jsonl rows: a list of {path, phrase} naming the lines that encode the belief?
decisions.recommended: Yes. It is the one missing join key. Today F-rows cite ADRs, specs and runs, and asm rows cite depends_on_it paths, but nothing points at a line, so no tool can go from a line to its belief.
options: derive anchors by text search only (no field)
decisions.why: A phrase survives line moves and rewording of nearby text; a line number goes stale on the next edit above it. Text search alone cannot tell two uses of the same words apart.

decisions.question: Report a belief's exit on both axes: truth (falsified, or still held) and liveness (moot, superseded), and for a falsified belief say whether the world changed or the old belief was wrong all along?
decisions.recommended: Yes, as fields in the verdict, not prose. Gotcha 17's 2026-10-06 shift was revealed incompleteness: the merge-method setting existed on every plan the whole time; the belief that enforcement was impossible was false when written.
options: both axes plus world-change vs revealed-incompleteness
decisions.why: Memories claim-exit-lattice and defeasible-warrant: a falsified claim you correct, a moot claim you vacate and mark; calling a miss a change hides the miss.

decisions.question: Fix the blindspot the trace found (scripts/squash_merge_detector.py line 7 still says branch protection cannot enforce the policy) as its own one-line docs PR, citing commit 1c798b7b?
decisions.recommended: Yes, separately and after this proposal, so the fix is the first receipt that cites a belief-blame finding.
options: leave it, the setting already enforces
decisions.why: The detector still works; only its stated reason is stale. A stale reason misleads the next reader into thinking the detector is the only guard.

decisions.question: Should a Tuition note in a script header that repeats a falsified belief be required to cite its F-row (and, when none exists, mint one)?
decisions.recommended: Yes, as a warning first (control K2), then a gate after 30 days if the false-positive rate is low.
decisions.why: F26 and the safe_merge.sh Tuition are the same failure three months apart. The ledger had the lesson; the fix did not carry it, so the class came back.

decisions.question: Where does belief blame render first?
decisions.recommended: CLI only (a read-only script with --self-test), then feed the WORLD.md HUD Time layer, which already promises belief change scrubbed by date with a falsified belief as a gold seam.
decisions.why: The HUD needs the join to exist before it can draw it. A visual that cannot go flat on empty data is decoration.

tables.title: The join: line, then commit, then assumption, then evidence
tables.intro: Each hop uses a source the repo already keeps. The only new key is anchors (D1).
rows: Which assumption does this line encode?
_STATE/assumptions.jsonl and _STATE/falsification-ledger.jsonl, field anchors (new); fallback depends_on_it paths
Match the line's text against each anchor phrase for that path. No match prints UNREGISTERED: the line holds a belief nobody wrote down.
git blame -w -C -L for the last touch, then git log -L on the line and git log -S on the anchor phrase to reach the first commit that stated it. Report both: entered_in and last_touched_in.

falsification-ledger rows; assumptions rows with decided_ref or supersedes; decision_receipt rows with supersedes (append-only chain); kintsugi seams in _PATTERNS/kintsugi-visual-grammar-seams.md; Tuition notes in script headers
Collect every row whose anchors, refs or text name the assumption or the line's path, ordered by date. Each one is a shift event with its own commit or receipt id.
Still current, or a known blindspot?
the rows from hop 3 plus the current text of every anchored line
CURRENT, SHIFTED-PROPAGATED, SHIFTED-STALE-SIBLING, RELAPSED, MOOT or UNREGISTERED (table below).
Same four questions for a backlog dependency

git log -S on the edge ("depends_on" with the target id) gives the commit that added it; its assumption is that the target must finish first; evidence is the target's state history and any row that superseded it.

tables.title: Verdicts
tables.intro: Truth and liveness are separate axes (D2). Every verdict prints the commit or row id that decided it.
rows: No evidence row shifted it, or every shift was a hold.
Evidence shifted it and every anchored line now states the new belief.
none; the gold seam is drawn
Evidence shifted it and one line was rewritten, but another anchored line still states the old belief.

A falsified belief failed again later and the later record does not cite the earlier row.

The question retired (the tool or rule was removed or superseded) rather than being answered false.
vacate and mark, do not correct
The line encodes a belief with no assumptions or F-row anchored to it.

tables.title: Worked example: AGENTS.md gotcha 17 (line 148 at main@ce13ec16)
tables.intro: Every value below was read from git and the ledgers in this worktree on 2026-11-01.
rows: Two beliefs share the line. A: a squash or rebase erases the per-PR boundary that receipts cite, so merge commits only. B (2026-09-28 wording): branch protection cannot enforce this on the free private plan, so a daily detector is the guard. No asm or F-row is anchored to either, so both print UNREGISTERED today.
git blame -w -C credits 51ddf069 (2026-10-20). git log -L walks back: 1c798b7b (2026-10-06), then 0df06046 (2026-09-28), the commit that first stated both beliefs.

2026-10-06: the repo's merge-method setting (allow_squash_merge and allow_rebase_merge false) enforces the ban on any plan. AGENTS.md was rewritten to say so. The setting existed all along, so this is revealed incompleteness, not a world change.
scripts/squash_merge_detector.py line 7 still says branch protection cannot enforce the policy, so detection, not prevention. git log -S on that phrase shows 1c798b7b removed it from AGENTS.md only.

A third belief rides the same line since 51ddf069: a merge gate must wait for every check to SUCCEED. F26 (2026-07-24) falsified "gh pr checks --watch then merge is enough" after PR 130 merged on red. The safe_merge.sh Tuition (2026-10-20) records PR 1722 merging while Vercel was PENDING. safe_merge.sh does not cite F26.

A CURRENT. B SHIFTED-STALE-SIBLING (fix: D3). The check-gate belief RELAPSED once, now held by safe_merge.sh; F26's fix text ("the only gate on free-tier private GitHub") is itself partly stale since 1c798b7b.

controls.name: Stale sibling
controls.plain: When an evidence row or commit rewrote one anchored line, every other line anchored to the same belief must no longer contain the old phrase.
controls.bad: Fixture: two files anchored to belief B, one rewritten at 1c798b7b, the other still containing "Branch protection cannot enforce" (a copy of scripts/squash_merge_detector.py at ce13ec16). Must print SHIFTED-STALE-SIBLING with both paths and 1c798b7b.
controls.good: The same fixture with the detector line rewritten prints SHIFTED-PROPAGATED.
controls.assay_ready: fixtures to be written first in the script's --self-test (temp git repo, two commits)

controls.name: Relapse without citation
controls.plain: A Tuition note or kintsugi seam that matches a FALSIFIED F-row's claim, dated after it, must cite that F-row.
controls.bad: Fixture: an F-row like F26 (2026-07-24, merge on red check) and a script header Tuition dated 2026-10-20 describing a merge on a PENDING check with no F-id. Must print RELAPSED naming both.
controls.good: The same Tuition with "(see F26)" prints nothing.
controls.assay_ready: matching is by anchors first, then by a shared anchor path; no fuzzy text match in the gate, so recall is low by design and false positives near zero
controls.threshold: known-bad flagged, known-good silent; warn only for 30 days (D4)

controls.name: Entry is not last touch
controls.plain: The reported entry commit is the first commit that stated the anchor phrase, not the git blame commit.
controls.bad: Fixture: a temp repo where commit 1 adds a line with the phrase and commit 2 rewords other words on the same line. Reporting commit 2 as entered_in fails.
controls.good: entered_in is commit 1, last_touched_in is commit 2. On the real repo, AGENTS.md gotcha 17 reports entered 0df06046, last touched 51ddf069.

human: When evidence changes your mind about a process rule, say which file states the old belief; the harness rewrites every sibling, not only the one in front of it.
Ask "did the world change, or were we wrong all along?" A miss called a change is a miss repeated.
A verdict of UNREGISTERED is not a defect; it is a belief nobody wrote a test for. Register it only if being wrong would cost something.
agent: Never report the git blame commit as when a belief entered; walk git log -L and git log -S on the anchor phrase.
Never edit a decided ledger row to record a shift; append a new row that points back (supersedes).
When you rewrite a process line because of new evidence, grep for the old phrase across the repo in the same change and cite the evidence id in the commit.
Belief blame is read-only. It prints verdicts; fixes go through the normal PR, merge and receipt path.

glossary.plain: A lookup that answers, for one line or one depends_on edge: which assumption, entered when, shifted by what evidence, current or not.
A {path, phrase} pair on a ledger row naming a line that states the belief. A phrase, never a line number, so it survives edits above it.
A second line that still states a belief after evidence rewrote the first one.
A falsified belief that fails again later, recorded without citing the earlier falsification.
The belief was false when written; new evidence only exposed it. Opposite of a world change, where it was true then and is false now.
The incident note at the top of a script header recording what went wrong and what the script now prevents.
The question retired, so the belief is vacated and marked rather than corrected.
